items.title: Energy price cap rise: how to switch providers
items.desc: It is possible to switch to a better tariff and save money despite the forecast rise next year Average energy bill in Great Britain predicted to rise to £2,166 The energy price cap in Great Britain looks likely to go up by 26% in January . But your bills might not have to rise by the same amount. If you are paying a tariff that matches the price cap you could save by switching to something lower. And if you do it now, you could make a substantial saving. Providers are offering fixed tariffs that work out up to £407 below the estimated price cap, according to price comparison website uSwitch. It’s worth noting that it’s the price of the energy you use that is fixed, not your bill – so you will still be charged according to what you use. Continue reading...

items.title: Doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby was barred from treating patients during trial
items.desc: Exclusive: Jury was never told that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was barred from practising over concerns for patients’ safety A senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety. Prof Peter Hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that the British nurse had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Jurors were never told. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year
items.desc: Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human. Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”. Continue reading...

items.title: Can Labour end the youth unemployment crisis? – podcast
items.desc: There are about a million young people across the country not in employment, education or training. Could Alan Milburn’s landmark report help change that? Richard Partington reports The UK has one of the worst rates in Europe when it comes to youth unemployment. From the savage cuts to youth services during austerity, to the impacts of the pandemic and now the threat of AI to entry level jobs, young people across the country are feeling that the social contract is broken. But now Alan Milburn, the 68-year-old New Labour veteran, has published a radical review urging the government to spend billions on a new deal for young people. Continue reading...
